\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Deciding with advice within a time bound]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.DecidesWithAdviceInTime}
\statementsource{Yap83}{
  pdf-1a201b302069-p002-b002,
  pdf-1a201b302069-p003-b002
}
\statementsource{Vad12}{
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p057-b006,
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p058-b002
}
\label{Turing.FinTM.DecidesWithAdviceInTime}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator, Turing.pairEncode}
Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $L$ be a language of
Boolean words, and let $\alpha$ and $T$ assign a Boolean list and a natural number,
respectively, to each input length. The machine decides $L$ with advice $\alpha$ within
time $T$ if, for every Boolean word $x$, on the encoded pair consisting of $x$ and
$\alpha(|x|)$ it computes within $T(|x|)$ steps the one-symbol output indicating whether
$x$ belongs to $L$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Time complexity with advice]
\lean{Complexity.DTIMEAdvice}
\statementsource{Yap83}{pdf-1a201b302069-p003-b002}
\statementsource{Vad12}{
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p057-b006,
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p058-b002
}
\label{Complexity.DTIMEAdvice}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.DecidesWithAdviceInTime}
For functions $T,a\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$, this class consists of languages of
Boolean words for which there are a constant $c\in\mathbb{N}$, an advice function
$\alpha\colon\mathbb{N}\to\{\text{Boolean lists}\}$, and a finite Turing machine such
that $|\alpha(n)|=a(n)$ for every $n$, and the machine decides the language with advice
$\alpha$ within time $cT$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of time with advice]
\lean{Complexity.DTIMEAdvice.mono}
\label{Complexity.DTIMEAdvice.mono}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.DTIMEAdvice, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.mono}
\difficulty{3}
Let $T_1,T_2,A : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ satisfy $T_1(n) \le T_2(n)$ for every $n$.
Then $\mathrm{DTIMEAdvice}(T_1,A) \subseteq \mathrm{DTIMEAdvice}(T_2,A)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Polynomial time with polynomial advice]
\lean{Complexity.PAdvicePoly}
\statementsource{Yap83}{
  pdf-1a201b302069-p003-b002,
  pdf-1a201b302069-p003-b006
}
\statementsource{Vad12}{
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p054-b004,
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p058-b002,
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p058-b003
}
\label{Complexity.PAdvicePoly}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.DTIMEAdvice}
This class is the union, over natural numbers $c,C,d$, of the languages decidable with
advice in time $n\mapsto n^c+1$ using advice of length $n\mapsto C(n+1)^d$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial advice class inclusion]
\lean{Complexity.DTIMEAdvice_subset_PAdvicePoly}
\label{Complexity.DTIMEAdvice_subset_PAdvicePoly}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.DTIMEAdvice, Complexity.PAdvicePoly}
\difficulty{3}
For all natural numbers $c,C,d$, every language decidable with advice of length
$C(n+1)^d$ in time bounded by a constant multiple of $n^c+1$ belongs to the class of
languages decidable with polynomially bounded advice and polynomial time.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Length of a doubled bit list]
\lean{Complexity.length_doubled}
\label{Complexity.length_doubled}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
For every finite bit string $x$, the list obtained by replacing each bit by two
consecutive copies has length $2|x|$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Scaling the time bound with advice]
\lean{Complexity.DTIMEAdvice.mono_const}
\label{Complexity.DTIMEAdvice.mono_const}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.DTIMEAdvice, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.mono}
\difficulty{3}
Let $T_1,T_2,A : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and $a \in \mathbb{N}$ satisfy $T_1(n) \le a
T_2(n)$ for every $n$. Then $\mathrm{DTIMEAdvice}(T_1,A) \subseteq
\mathrm{DTIMEAdvice}(T_2,A)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Zero-time advice classes are empty]
\lean{Complexity.DTIMEAdvice_eq_empty_of_eq_zero}
\label{Complexity.DTIMEAdvice_eq_empty_of_eq_zero}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.DTIMEAdvice, Turing.FinTM.computesInTime_iff, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom}
\difficulty{4}
Let $T,a : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, and suppose $T(0)=0$. Then the class of languages
decidable with advice in time bounded by a constant multiple of $T$ is empty, regardless
of the advice-length function $a$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Positive-power advice classes are empty]
\lean{Complexity.DTIMEAdvice_pow_eq_empty}
\label{Complexity.DTIMEAdvice_pow_eq_empty}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.DTIMEAdvice, Complexity.DTIMEAdvice_eq_empty_of_eq_zero}
\difficulty{1}
Let $c$ be a nonzero natural number and let $a : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be an
advice-length function. The class of languages decidable with advice in time bounded by
a constant multiple of $n^c$ is empty.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial advice-time classes]
\lean{Complexity.iUnion_DTIMEAdvice_pow_eq}
\label{Complexity.iUnion_DTIMEAdvice_pow_eq}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.DTIMEAdvice, Complexity.DTIMEAdvice_pow_eq_empty}
\difficulty{4}
The union, over all natural numbers $c$ and $d$, of the classes of languages decidable
with advice of length $n^d$ in time bounded by a constant multiple of $n^c$ equals the
union, over all natural numbers $d$, of the classes of languages decidable with advice
of length $n^d$ in constant time up to a constant factor.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Zero-length advice equals deterministic time]
\lean{Complexity.DTIMEAdvice_zero_eq_DTIME}
\label{Complexity.DTIMEAdvice_zero_eq_DTIME}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.DTIME, Complexity.DTIMEAdvice, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.mono, Turing.FinTM.bufferedCompTM, Turing.FinTM.bufferedCompTM_computesInTime, Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_const, Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_pairDup, Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_pairFst, Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_pairMapSnd, Turing.length_pairEncode, Turing.pairDecode_pairEncode, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{6}
Let $T : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ satisfy $n+1 \le T(n)$ for every natural number $n$.
Then the class of languages decidable with advice of length zero in time bounded by a
constant multiple of $T$ equals the deterministic time class defined by $T$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Zero-length advice and polynomial time]
\lean{Complexity.iUnion_DTIMEAdvice_zero_eq_P}
\label{Complexity.iUnion_DTIMEAdvice_zero_eq_P}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.DTIMEAdvice, Complexity.DTIMEAdvice.mono_const, Complexity.DTIMEAdvice_zero_eq_DTIME, Complexity.P, Complexity.dtime_poly_subset_P, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.mono}
\difficulty{5}
The union, over all natural numbers $c$, of the classes of languages decidable with
advice of length zero in time bounded by a constant multiple of $n^c+1$ is exactly the
class of polynomial-time decidable languages.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial time with polynomial advice]
\lean{Complexity.P_subset_PAdvicePoly}
\label{Complexity.P_subset_PAdvicePoly}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.DTIMEAdvice_subset_PAdvicePoly, Complexity.P, Complexity.PAdvicePoly, Complexity.iUnion_DTIMEAdvice_zero_eq_P}
\difficulty{3}
Every binary language decidable in polynomial time belongs to the class of languages
decidable in polynomial time when supplied with an advice string whose length is
polynomial in the input length.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Right-moving machine action]
\lean{Complexity.aoMove}
\label{Complexity.aoMove}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action}
For each state $q'$ in a four-element state set, define a one-step action for a machine
with no work tapes over the Boolean alphabet: it moves the input head right, emits no
output symbol, and has successor state $q'$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Halting output action]
\lean{Complexity.aoHalt}
\label{Complexity.aoHalt}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action}
For each Boolean value $b$, define an action for a machine with no work tapes and
Boolean output symbols whose state set has four elements: it stays on the input tape,
emits $b$, and halts immediately.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Advice machine transition rule]
\lean{Complexity.aoTr}
\label{Complexity.aoTr}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.aoHalt, Complexity.aoMove, Turing.Action}
For a machine with four states, no work tapes, and Boolean input and output symbols,
define its transition as follows. In state $0$, on input $1$ it moves to state $1$, on
input $0$ it moves to state $2$, and on a blank it halts emitting $0$. In state $1$, on
either Boolean input it moves to state $0$, and on a blank it halts emitting $0$. In
state $2$, on input $1$ it moves to state $3$, and on input $0$ or a blank it halts
emitting $0$. In state $3$, on input $b$ it halts emitting $b$, and on a blank it halts
emitting $0$. In every transition to another state, it uses the action denoted by the
corresponding move.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Advice ones machine]
\lean{Complexity.adviceOnesTM}
\label{Complexity.adviceOnesTM}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.aoTr, Turing.FinTM}
Define a deterministic Turing machine with Boolean input and four states, no work tapes,
and initial state $0$, whose transition rule is the one specified for the advice machine
above.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Advice machine configuration]
\lean{Complexity.aoCfg}
\label{Complexity.aoCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg}
For a Boolean input word $w$, a state $q$ among four states, and a natural number $p$,
define a configuration with state $q$, empty work tapes, and empty output. Its input
head is at position $\min(p, |w|+1)$ among the $|w|+2$ positions, indexed from $0$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[One-step transition of the advice machine]
\lean{Complexity.ao_step}
\label{Complexity.ao_step}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.adviceOnesTM, Complexity.aoCfg, Complexity.aoTr, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.inputSymbolInner}
\difficulty{3}
Let $w$ be a finite bit string, let $q$ be one of four states, and let $i<|w|$. One step
of the fixed advice-ones machine from state $q$ with its input head at position $i+1$ is
exactly the configuration obtained by applying to that configuration the action
prescribed by the machine's transition rule for state $q$ and the bit at position $i$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Input-head advance of the advice machine]
\lean{Complexity.ao_move}
\label{Complexity.ao_move}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.adviceOnesTM, Complexity.aoCfg, Complexity.aoMove, Complexity.aoTr, Complexity.ao_step, Turing.Cfg.ext_zero_tapes, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.moveInputPos, Turing.moveInputPos_pos_of_ne_right}
\difficulty{4}
Let $w$ be a finite bit string, let $q,q'$ be states among four states, and let $i<|w|$.
If the bit at position $i$ is $v$ and the transition of the fixed advice-ones machine
from $q$ on input bit $v$ is the action that moves to state $q'$, then one step from
state $q$ with its input head at position $i+1$ yields the configuration with state $q'$
and input head at position $i+2$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Halting and output of the advice machine]
\lean{Complexity.ao_halt}
\label{Complexity.ao_halt}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.adviceOnesTM, Complexity.aoCfg, Complexity.aoHalt, Complexity.aoTr, Complexity.ao_step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step}
\difficulty{3}
Let $w$ be a finite bit string, let $q$ be one of four states, and let $i<|w|$. If the
bit $v$ is at position $i$ and the transition of the fixed advice-ones machine from
state $q$ on input bit $v$ is the action that emits $b$ and halts, then one step from
state $q$ with its input head at position $i+1$ halts and outputs the one-bit string
$b$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Indexed entries of a duplicated bit string]
\lean{Complexity.doubled_getElem?}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $x$ be a finite bit string and let $p$ be a natural number. In the string formed by
replacing each bit of $x$ by two consecutive copies, the entries at indices $2p$ and
$2p+1$ are both equal to the entry of $x$ at index $p$, with out-of-range lookups
interpreted as absent.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Positions in a Pair Encoding]
\lean{Complexity.pairEncode_getElem?}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.doubled_getElem?, Complexity.length_doubled, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{4}
For binary strings $x,\alpha$, each bit $x_p$ with $p<|x|$ occurs at both positions $2p$
and $2p+1$ of $\langle x,\alpha\rangle$. Positions $2|x|$ and $2|x|+1$ contain $0$ and
$1$, respectively, and for every $i\in\mathbb{N}$ the bit at position $2|x|+2+i$ equals
$\alpha_i$; out-of-range positions are interpreted as undefined.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[List lookup yields an indexed entry]
\lean{Complexity.getElem_of_getElem?_eq}
\leanok
\difficulty{1}
Let $w$ be a Boolean list, let $i$ be a natural number, and let $v$ be Boolean. If the
optional lookup of $w$ at index $i$ returns $v$, then $i$ is less than the length of $w$
and the entry of $w$ at index $i$ is $v$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Boolean words equal to one from a position]
\lean{Complexity.onesFrom}
\label{Complexity.onesFrom}
\leanok
For a Boolean word $x$ and a natural number $p$, the property that all entries of $x$ at
indices $j \ge p$ are true is defined to mean that for every index $j<|x|$ with $p\le
j$, the entry $x_j$ equals true.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Scan test for a suffix of ones]
\lean{Complexity.ao_scan}
\label{Complexity.ao_scan}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.adviceOnesTM, Complexity.aoCfg, Complexity.ao_halt, Complexity.ao_move, Complexity.getElem_of_getElem?_eq, Complexity.onesFrom, Complexity.pairEncode_getElem?, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_of_halt, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step, Turing.length_pairEncode, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{6}
Let $x$ be a finite bit string and $b$ a bit. For all natural numbers $r,p$ such that
$|x|=p+r$, run the fixed advice-ones machine for $2r+3$ steps on the self-delimiting
encoding of $x$ followed by the one-bit string $[b]$, starting in state $0$ with its
input head at position $2p+1$. The resulting configuration is halted and its output is
the one-bit string whose value is true exactly when $b$ is true and every bit of $x$ at
an index $j$ with $p\le j<|x|$ is true.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Advice complexity of sublanguages of all ones]
\lean{Complexity.mem_DTIMEAdvice_one_of_le_allOnes}
\label{Complexity.mem_DTIMEAdvice_one_of_le_allOnes}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.DTIMEAdvice, Complexity.adviceOnesTM, Complexity.aoCfg, Complexity.ao_scan, Complexity.onesFrom, Language.allOnes, Language.mem_allOnes_iff, Turing.Cfg.ext_zero_tapes, Turing.Cfg.init, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.mono, Turing.FinTM.computesInTime_iff, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{5}
Let $L$ be a language of finite binary words. If every word in $L$ consists entirely of
ones, then there is a natural number $c$ such that a finite Turing machine decides $L$
with advice of exactly one bit at each input length and running time at most $c(n+1)$ on
inputs of length $n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Advice polynomial time for all-ones sublanguages]
\lean{Complexity.mem_PAdvicePoly_of_le_allOnes}
\label{Complexity.mem_PAdvicePoly_of_le_allOnes}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.DTIMEAdvice_subset_PAdvicePoly, Complexity.PAdvicePoly, Complexity.mem_DTIMEAdvice_one_of_le_allOnes, Language.allOnes}
\difficulty{4}
Let $L$ be a language over the binary alphabet such that every word in $L$ consists
entirely of $1$s. Then $L$ belongs to polynomial time with polynomial-length advice:
there are natural numbers $c,C,d$, an advice string of length exactly $C(n+1)^d$ for
each input length $n$, and a finite Turing machine that decides membership in $L$ on
input paired with its length-$|x|$ advice within $c(|x|^c+1)$ steps.
\end{theorem}
